closest_works.citation: Sekine (2026), In Defence of Second-Order Reasons, section 3
closest_works.shared_claim: Psychological possibility of reason exclusion; this exact three-rate experiment.
closest_works.difference: Explicit pair of observationally equivalent models refutes a specific positive inference to some individual successful excluders; does not reject conceptual defence.

closest_works.shared_claim: Partial discounting differs from discarding; same experiment warrants statistical caution. These are inherited prior findings.
closest_works.difference: Structural non-identification persists even for exact population rates, and unchanged individual verdicts still do not identify the basing relation; directed against Sekine’s later inference, not a new caution about significance.

closest_works.shared_claim: Acting for a reason for a reason involves more than matching an outcome.
closest_works.difference: No novel account of basing claimed; applies distinction to invalidate a concrete empirical identification step with constructive countermodels.

closest_works.shared_claim: Cognitive limitations challenge practical reason exclusion.
closest_works.difference: Proposal neither declares impossibility nor reinvents this challenge; tests the evidential bridge from output rates to full individual exclusion. Incomplete access limits comparison.

closest_works.shared_claim: Group causal information does not automatically identify individual causal effects. General methodological background is inherited.
closest_works.difference: No new statistical theorem; exact correction to a philosophical argument plus distinction between outcome invariance and reason-guided basing.

limitations: Self-assessment only; independent precheck required. Target Sekine and closest Wittlin passages directly read. Wistrich original full paper inaccessible: critique grants Sekine’s numerical premises, no raw-data inference. Rocchè/Wang full texts inaccessible; Holland abstract only. No exhaustive priority claim. Novelty rests on concrete local correction beyond known aggregate/individual and discount/discard distinctions; critic may reject its significance.
